title: Quantum Computing Gains Commercial Traction, Revenue Seen At $1.1 Bn In 2027: Gartner
key_facts: Gartner projects global quantum computing revenue of USD 1.1 billion in 2027, up from USD 869.9 million in 2026.
It expects 22.9 per cent growth in 2026.
The public sector stays the biggest spender through 2027: USD 245 million in 2027 against USD 219 million in 2026.
Banking, financial services and insurance is forecast to overtake the public sector from 2028: USD 289 million against USD 280 million.
Gartner expects more than 50 per cent of quantum computing startups to exit the market by 2030 as the field consolidates.
Gartner advises CIOs to treat quantum as a multiyear effort.
quote_evidence: Global quantum computing revenue is projected to reach USD 1.1 billion in 2027, up from USD 869.9 million in 2026, according to Gartner.
The banking, financial services and insurance (BFI) sector is expected to overtake the public sector as the largest source of quantum computing spending from 2028.
The research firm said the market is currently overcrowded and expects more than 50 per cent of quantum computing startups to exit the market.
why_it_matters_hint: A respected analyst firm sees quantum revenue still small but growing, with many startups expected to fail.
notes: Gartner forecast, a projection and not a measurement. Original Gartner press release not read.
